meta_title: GrubMarket AI Alternative for Distributors in 2026
meta_desc: Keep GrubAssist for your team and hand your customers a voice app too: they speak and approve each order. A GrubMarket AI alternative that keeps GrubAssist.

hero.h1: GrubMarket AI Alternative? Hand Customers The Microphone.
hero.lead: Put a microphone in your customers' hands as well. VoiceOrder Solutions runs beside GrubAssist: the kitchen speaks the order into our app on its own phone, approves each line, and it reaches your desk finished. Your team keeps its assistant for questions about the business.

problem.h2: Why teams want an alternative to GrubMarket AI
problem.lead: GrubMarket AI calls GrubAssist a virtual assistant for the food supply chain, and the jobs it advertises are business analysis, performance, cash flow and spotting anomalies, with order creation among them. All useful, and worth keeping. A GrubMarket AI alternative search usually starts from one gap: the customer still sends a message for somebody to interpret.

cards.h3: Their site describes an assistant for your team
cards.body: The jobs GrubAssist advertises are ones a distributor's team does: looking into the numbers and writing up orders. However quick that makes entry, it is not the same as the order arriving already built by the person who wanted it.

cards.h3: Extraction starts from a loose message
cards.body: Their order extraction reads voicemail, email and text messages at any hour, which is useful. Each one still begins as a message, though, and the kitchen that sent it never sees the lines it became.

cards.h3: The assistant is the part worth keeping
cards.body: If GrubAssist already tells your team how accounts are trending, swapping it out to change how ordering works would throw away the bit that does its job.

cards.h2: GrubAssist for your team, VoiceOrder Solutions for your customers
cards.lead: We are not a GrubMarket AI replacement and do not try to be. Our app covers the customer end, so the tool your staff rely on is left alone.

items.h3: Keep the assistant for the questions
items.body: Asking out loud how a customer is trending, or where the cash is, is a genuinely useful thing and we cannot do it. Keep it for those questions, and let the customer build the order.

items.h3: Shrink the pile that needs extracting
items.body: Each account you move across sends a structured, approved order rather than a voicemail. Whatever is doing the extracting keeps handling the messages that still arrive.

items.h3: One place for it to land, whatever else you run
items.body: Sent over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, ours reach the same software as everything else, so nobody ends up with two places to look.

midcta.body: Twenty minutes. A buyer speaks an order, approves it, and it arrives on the desk as a PDF, over EDI or over the API.

faq.h2: Better than GrubMarket AI, or the other half of it?

items.q: Do I need a GrubMarket AI alternative so customers can speak their own orders?
items.a: No. GrubAssist can keep serving your team while VoiceOrder Solutions gives each account its own route in: say it into our app, check it, send it. Nothing on your side has to be switched off or retrained.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions a GrubMarket AI competitor, since both use voice?
items.a: Less than it looks. GrubAssist, going by their own site, works for your team: ask it about the business, have it write up an order. Ours is for your customers, who speak and approve their own orders, so your staff never build the ones sent through our app. That is why a team looking at a GrubMarket AI alternative over voice can simply run both.

items.q: Can your app tell us how a customer is performing?
items.a: No. Our admin screen shows what each account has ordered and lets you manage accounts and guides. Reporting on how accounts perform is on their list, not ours, which is a good reason to keep GrubAssist.

items.q: Is there any link between GrubAssist and your app?
items.a: None. Nothing links the two, and neither company supports the other. GrubAssist connects to your ERP so it can answer questions about the business; we only ever deliver approved orders into your system, in the formats listed further up.

items.q: Do we have to teach your app our catalog?
items.a: No, and there is no module for it, because nothing has to be taught. The item list you keep for an account is the configuration. GrubMarket AI ships an AI training module for its assistant, and that stays theirs to run.

items.q: How soon could our accounts be ordering?
items.a: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, and a first order usually follows the day each login arrives. GrubAssist carries on as before while it happens. Accounts that keep calling still can; a call just gets no order number or timestamp from us.

items.q: How is voice for customers priced next to GrubAssist?
items.a: Neither of us publishes a figure. Ours arrives as a quote once we know your setup; theirs comes after a demo. Keeping GrubAssist means the number to weigh is only what the voice app for accounts adds.

items.q: Where do the GrubMarket details on this page come from?
items.a: Taken from grubmarket.ai on 10 October 2026, which is the GrubMarket AI product rather than GrubMarket the company: the GrubAssist description, the list of advertised jobs, the training module and the other products all come off that page. They publish no price and no rollout time, so this page does not guess at either. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.
